In an experiment to determine the Young modulus E of the material of a wire, the measurements
taken are shown.
mass hung on end of wire
m = 2.300 ± 0.002 kg
original length of wire
l = 2.864 ± 0.005 m
diameter of wire
d = 0.82 ± 0.01 mm
extension of wire
e = 7.6 ± 0.2 mm
The Young modulus is calculated using
E
e
d
mg

4
π
=
l
where g is the acceleration of free fall.
N m–2.
The calculated value of E is 1.61 × 1010
How should the calculated value of E and its uncertainty be expressed?
N m–2
A
(1.61 ± 0.04) × 1010
N m–2
B
(1.61 ± 0.05) × 1010
N m–2
C
(1.61 ± 0.07) × 1010
N m–2
D
(1.61 ± 0.09) × 1010

hints: Notice $E = 4mgl/(\pi d^2 e)$, so $m$, $l$ and $e$ appear to power 1 while $d$ appears as $d^2$.
Recall fractional uncertainties add in multiplication and division, and a power $x^n$ contributes $n$ times $\Delta x / x$.
walkthrough: Write the fractional uncertainty for $E$ from $E \propto m l / (d^2 e)$ as $\Delta E/E = \Delta m/m + \Delta l/l + 2\Delta d/d + \Delta e/e$.
Substitute the given values: $\Delta m/m = 0.002/2.300 \approx 0.00087$, $\Delta l/l = 0.005/2.864 \approx 0.00175$.
For the squared diameter, $2\Delta d/d = 2 \times 0.01/0.82 \approx 0.02439$, and for extension $\Delta e/e = 0.2/7.6 \approx 0.02632$.

Convert to absolute uncertainty: $\Delta E \approx 0.0533 \times 1.61 \times 10^{10} \approx 0.086 \times 10^{10} \text{ N m}^{-2}$, which rounds to $0.09 \times 10^{10} \text{ N m}^{-2}$ to match the value precision.
Hence $E = (1.61 \pm 0.09) \times 10^{10} \text{ N m}^{-2}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: Too small. It corresponds to about 2.5% and misses the full contributions from $d$ and $e$.

B.explanation: Too small. It omits the factor of 2 for $d^2$ and underestimates the $e = 7.6 \pm 0.2 \text{ mm}$ term.

C.explanation: Too small. It is close to adding $2 \times 0.01/0.82$ and $0.2/7.6$ only, without the small $m$ and $l$ terms.

D.explanation: Correct. Total fractional uncertainty is about 5.3%, giving $0.09 \times 10^{10} \text{ N m}^{-2}$ on $1.61 \times 10^{10} \text{ N m}^{-2}$.
